candidates.api: from pycparserext.ext_c_parser import OpenCLCParser; OpenCLCParser().parse(text, filename='', debuglevel=0, initial_type_symbols=frozenset())
candidates.output: pycparser.c_ast.FileAST. Definitions use FuncDef and Decl. Syntactic calls use FuncCall(name, args, coord); a direct callee is an ID. OpenCL kernel, address-space and access qualifiers remain declaration function/qualifier strings.
candidates.locations: Coord contains file, line and optional column only. It has no end position or byte offsets.
candidates.semantic_limit: No typechecking, name binding, call resolution or file resolution is exposed.
candidates.preprocessing: OpenCLCParser.parse consumes text. Realistic sources require preprocessed input; pycparser.parse_file may be given parser=OpenCLCParser(), use_cpp=True and an explicit preprocessor command/options.

candidates.source_frontend: For .cl input the implementation invokes clang -c -x cl -emit-llvm -S -cl-std=CL2.0 -Xclang -finclude-default-header -fno-discard-value-names, then parses LLVM IR with llvmlite. It also accepts LLVM IR directly.
candidates.output: A mapping from LLVM argument spelling/type to input, output or input/output; optional argument list. The CLI emits a table or CSV.
candidates.scope_limit: It analyzes one named kernel's argument I/O roles. It does not emit source definitions, calls or source ranges.
candidates.route: Keep as an untried semantic adjunct. Its use of Clang is a dependency and scope fact, not a measured failure or reason to discard it.
